about: An underground-cavern endgame: a final test set by an old silver-haired man. You start at the foot of an endless stair and cross a shadowy land, where you face a hooded double of yourself. A sea, a lake and an aqueduct lie beyond, but most exits are blocked by rockfalls, squeezes or surf.

done.why: Every other exit was blocked with a 'not today' message. The only lead was the sailor on the ship. The ship never came back after one pass, however long I waited or however often I re-entered the shore.

ending.what: None reached. The furthest I got was the Flathead Ocean shore and the Aqueduct View balcony.

moments.note: The sword leaps into my hand and a cloaked duelist appears.
Removing the hood of the beaten figure shows my own face, then an old man's. A strong moment.
The sailor says to greet him short and loud, but the ship passes once and never returns.
The paths north, east and northwest all say 'not today'. Almost all of the map is closed off.
I waited about 20 turns for the ship with no result.

wished: A way to hail the ship with words it understands, or a clear sign of when it returns.
Some hint of what makes me worthy of the old man's test.

lines.line: hangs within reach of your hand.
lines.why: It hints at the mercy choice: unmask the beaten foe rather than finish it.

lines.line: recoil in horror at the sight of your own face, weary and wounded.
lines.why: The emotional high point of the session.

fun.why: The duel and unmasking were good. After that I was stuck behind blocked exits.

engagement.why: Strong start, then it faded once progress stopped.

difficulty.why: The way forward was unclear and the ship's timing was opaque.

interestingness.why: The self-duel and the aqueduct's melancholy give it atmosphere.

prose.why: Evocative lines, such as the water 'cold that would open your hands'.
